- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at +3–4 points above peak.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in downward trends — add 0.5–1.5 points to forecast if recent price is falling below 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.5 points to forecast to catch momentum.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to adjust — use median of recent 5–7 day prices as baseline for correction.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment confirms strong reversal (e.g., >2 consecutive bearish sentiment values).
